summary: Ronald Egan is a sinologist who earned his Ph.D. from Harvard University. He held posts at Harvard (~1978–1987), Wellesley College (~1987–1991), UC Santa Barbara as Professor of Chinese Literature (~1991–2012), and Stanford University (~2012).

Ronald Eric Emmerick (1937–2001) specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He earned his Ph.D. from Oxford in 1964, studied under Harold Walter Bailey (~1961–1965), and served as Professor at the University of Hamburg from 1971 to 2001.

Ronald M. Davidson works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology, earning his PhD from UC Berkeley in 1985. He studied under numerous scholars, including Padmanabh S. Jaini and Lewis Lancaster, and held an attested post at Fairfield University (2002–2005).

Ronald Neufeldt (born 1941) is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He held a long-term post at the University of Calgary (~1977–2006), where he served as Associate Professor in the Religious Studies Department around 1977.

Ronald Y. Nakasone is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1975–1980). He held posts at the Institute of Buddhist Studies as an assistant professor (~1987) and at the Pacific School of Religion (attested 1996).
Rong Geng (1894–1983) was a scholar of sinology, history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Peking University (~1922–1925) and held a post at Yenching University (~1926–1946).

Rong Ma (born 1950) is a Tibetology and sociology scholar who earned a doctorate in social geography from Brown University. He was a visiting scholar at Harvard University and served as Director of Peking University's Institute of Sociology and Anthropology (attested 1998).

Rongdao Lai specializes in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. She earned her Ph.D. at McGill University (attested 2013) under doctoral supervisors G. Victor Sōgen Hori and Robin D. S. Yates, and was a visiting fellow at the Center for Chinese Studies.

Rory Lindsay is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Toronto and earned his PhD at Harvard University under Leonard van der Kuijp alongside numerous other teachers.
Rory Mackenzie is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who completed his doctoral studies under Peter Harvey. He held a teaching post at the International Christian College.

Rosalind O'Hanlon is an Indology and history scholar who earned her PhD from SOAS (~1978–1983). She was a Fellow at Clare College, Cambridge (~1985–2006), Professor in Indian History and Culture at Oxford (~2006–2020), and a British Academy Fellow (2020).

Rosan Ikeda (born 1941) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University (1960–1969). He held successive academic positions at Komazawa University from 1969 to 2012, including Professor (1983–2012), and became head of the Soto Zen Research Center in 2009.

Rosane Rocher (born 1937) is an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied under Ludo Rocher. She worked at the National Fund for Scientific Research (1961–1970), became a Professor at the University of Pennsylvania (1970), and headed the Rocher Foundation (~2013).

Rosemarie Fuchs (born 1950) is an active scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Katia Holmes and Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche, and served as a member of the Marpa Translation Committee (attested 2000).

Rosemarie Lühr (born 1946) is a linguist and Indologist who earned her doctorate under Karl Hoffmann at Erlangen-Nürnberg and habilitated at Regensburg. She held professorships at Giessen (1990–1994), Jena (1994–2013), and Humboldt University (2013).
Rosemary Radford Ruether (1936–2022) was a scholar in religious studies. She studied at Claremont School of Theology (~1960–1965) and held a post at Howard University (~1965–1975).

Rosina Pastore is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned her PhD at the University of Lausanne under doctoral supervisors Maya Burger and Stefania Cavaliere. She also served as an assistant and PhD candidate at Lausanne.

Ross Bolleter (born 1946) is a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar who earned a bachelor's degree at the University of Western Australia under David Tunley (~1964–1967). He served as a Zen Buddhist teacher at the Zen Group of Western Australia until 2023.

Roy Rappaport (1926–1997) was a religious studies scholar who earned his doctorate at Columbia University (~1959–1966). He served as Chair of the Department of Anthropology at the University of Michigan (~1965–1997) and past president of the American Anthropological Association (~1987–1989).

Roy Tzohar (born 1973) works in philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tel Aviv University (~1998–2005) and completed his PhD at Columbia University under Gary A. Tubb (~2005–2011), later joining Tel Aviv University (~2011).
